clue.text: Place in dive restricted pianist

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, sitting within the shortened word
something restricted is cut short, so the word for a dive loses its final letter

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or club, a joint
PL is the standard abbreviation for place in addresses

explanation.surface: Someone is playing piano in a cramped, seedy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Dive here is a noun for a low-class bar, not a plunge into water.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott Joplin was the American composer and ragtime piano player behind The Entertainer.

clue.text: Person in a minority?

parts.note: surface reading: someone belonging to a small group of the population
setter's reading: minority also means the state of being under legal age

explanation.walkthrough: Minority suggests a group outnumbered by others, but in law it is the period before adulthood.
explanation.definitionFit: A young person still under the age of legal majority is, technically, in their minority.

clue.text: Old college group embracing good skilled linguist

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the group word wraps around the letter for good

parts.note: short for polytechnic, a type of British college now renamed as universities
a lot is a group or batch
G is the usual abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A former college club includes someone very good at languages.
explanation.walkthrough: Polytechnics were British higher-education colleges, mostly converted to universities in 1992, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyglot speaks or understands many languages fluently.

clue.text: Pint's seen to be spilt? It's clumsy behaviour

indicators.note: spilt liquid ends up scattered, so the letters of these words are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the letters taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone notices a pint knocked over and calls it clumsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inept means lacking skill, so the noun covers awkward, bungling conduct.

clue.text: Peer against one small feature of boxing

parts.note: V for versus, as in a fixture listing
the Roman numeral for one
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
the referee counts to ten over a floored boxer

explanation.surface: A lord takes a stand against one detail of the boxing world.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscount is a member of the British nobility, ranking between earl and baron, so a peer.

clue.text: Basic silence after commotion beyond reach

indicators.note: a commotion is noisy disorder, so these words emerge from it in a jumbled order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: After an uproar, a plain quiet descends that nobody can disturb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be reached or approached is out of anyone's grasp.

clue.text: Trinket companion put on part of body

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
a limb of the body

explanation.surface: A friend fastens a little ornament on someone's wrist or arm.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one piece put on another sits above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm is a small ornament worn on a bracelet or chain, a trinket.

clue.text: Some sun is expected, in indiscriminate fashion?

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used, a run lying inside them

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the three words

explanation.surface: A weather forecast promises a little sunshine, scattered without favour.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: fashion here means clothing styles, which unisex ones do not sort by sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Unisex clothing is designed for both men and women, making no distinction between them.

clue.text: Fashionable Republican aim within limits of tolerability

indicators.note: the other pieces sit inside the edge letters
the limits of a word are its edges, its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
R is the abbreviation for Republican
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A political goal is pitched as stylish, as far as can be tolerated.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy describes what is in vogue or following the latest style.

clue.text: Discharge some court action

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a simultaneous firing of many guns
second meaning: a shot struck before the ball bounces on a tennis court

explanation.surface: Someone is released after a spell of legal proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: Court looks like a law court, which fits discharge; it is the tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a burst of gunfire and a tennis stroke hit in the air.

clue.text: Look mostly in state for source of firepower

indicators.note: the shortened word is placed inside the name of the state

parts.note: the US state in New England

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word for look drops its last letter

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily

explanation.surface: Someone peers around a state, hunting where the guns come from.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine is the chamber feeding cartridges into a gun, or a store of ammunition.

clue.text: For ages, a firm manufactured a dairy product

indicators.note: something manufactured is made up from raw material, so these letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A company has long produced some milk-based foodstuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Fromage frais is a soft, fresh French cheese, eaten like yoghurt.

clue.text: Man on board discussed time for retirement

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken about, so the answer is a word that is said like the chess piece

parts.note: a knight is a chessman, a piece on the board

explanation.surface: A chess player talks about when to give up the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement here is going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is when people retire, going to bed and sleeping.

clue.text: Advocate green measure amid split

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so these pieces go inside the word for split

parts.note: to rend is to tear apart
eco is the prefix for environmentally friendly
millimetres, a unit of measure

explanation.surface: Someone champions an environmental policy in the middle of a division.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate is to speak in favour of something, to recommend it.

clue.text: Millions see fantastic footballer

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or strange, so the letters come out in a strange arrangement

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Millions of fans watch a brilliant footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lionel Messi is the Argentine forward, a multiple Ballon d'Or winner who played for Barcelona.

clue.text: Getting round in time, I examine critically planned route

indicators.note: getting round something means encircling it, so the examining word wraps around the time phrase

parts.note: taken as written
to try a case is to examine it in court
taken as written
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A traveller, short of time, scrutinises their travel plan.
explanation.walkthrough: To try is the legal sense: a judge examines a case critically when trying it.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerary is the scheduled sequence of stops on a journey.

clue.text: Oak panelling popular within West Berkshire town

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for west

indicators.note: within means inside, so the word for popular sits inside the town's name

parts.note: Ascot is a town in Berkshire, England, famous for its racecourse
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A fashionable oak-lined interior in a town west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Wainscot is wooden lining on the lower walls of a room, traditionally made of oak.

clue.text: Sunday excursionist, one giving up habit

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday
a tripper is someone on a day trip

explanation.surface: A Sunday day-tripper is someone quitting a bad habit.
explanation.walkthrough: Habit suggests an addiction, or a nun's robe; here it is clothing taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripper removes clothes as a performance, and a habit is a garment.

clue.text: Telling number inspired by giant sci-fi works

indicators.note: to be inspired is to be breathed in, so the number letter is drawn inside the other words
the word works as a verb means operates on or kneads, so everything is reworked into a new order

parts.note: the letters taken as written, hyphen ignored
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A revealing figure is drawn from huge science-fiction books.
explanation.definitionFit: A telling detail is one that is revealing or meaningful, which is to say significant.

clue.text: Part of England not cold? It's part of Italy

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for cold is taken out

parts.note: Cumbria is the county of north-west England containing the Lake District
C for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A warm region of England turns out to be in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbria is the landlocked central Italian region around Perugia and Assisi.

clue.text: Second musician forgoing introduction

indicators.note: going without an introduction means losing the opening letter

parts.note: a bassist plays bass guitar or double bass

explanation.surface: A backing player skips being introduced to the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Second looks like a noun, a unit of time; here it is the verb meaning to back someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To second someone is to support or help them, as a second does in a duel.

clue.text: Imperious scholar worries about university lecturer

parts.note: a Master of Arts, a graduate scholar

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the word for worries is read from the end back to the start

parts.note: to fret is to worry
U is the abbreviation for university
L is the abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: A domineering academic frets over a university colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: Masterful and imperious both describe someone commanding and used to being obeyed.

clue.text: Host representing outsiders in music?

indicators.note: the outsiders of a word are the letters at its two edges

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A presenter stands in for the people outside the music scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters are written out as their spoken names, em and cee; MC stands for master of ceremonies.
explanation.definitionFit: An emcee is a master of ceremonies, the presenter who hosts an event.

clue.text: News in continental group, source of infinite boredom

indicators.note: the news letters are placed inside the group's abbreviation

parts.note: the European Union, a group on the Continent
N and N, two news letters: N is short for new, so News is N plus N

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: European news broadcasts generate endless tedium.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French loanword for listless weariness and lack of interest.

clue.text: Croatian is dressed in a waterproof

indicators.note: to dress is to arrange or prepare, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A man from Croatia wears a protective coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof is a British name for a coat that keeps out rain.

clue.text: Rash figure from chart about a part of the US

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the chart word goes round the rest

parts.note: a map is a chart
taken as written
the District of Columbia, home of Washington

explanation.surface: A reckless number has been read off a graph about America.
explanation.walkthrough: Figure looks like a number from the chart, but it is a person; madcap works as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap is a reckless, impulsive person, so a rash character.

clue.text: Theatrical star finally appearing in version of Cats? Yes

indicators.note: the selected letter shows up inside the other letters
a version is a rendering in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word before it, its last letter

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A star finally lands a part in a new staging of the musical Cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Actressy describes showy, affected behaviour like a stage performer's, so theatrical.

clue.text: Secretive type, one in bed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who reveals nothing, close as a clam
second meaning: a shellfish living on a seabed colony

explanation.surface: A discreet person keeps quiet about who they share a bed with.
explanation.walkthrough: Bed sounds like sleeping arrangements; an oyster bed is where the shellfish are farmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters stay tightly shut and are raised in beds, and a closed-mouthed person is called an oyster.
